decision: WF-127 models the two behaviours the research under-specifies: how a downstream viewer becomes a discovered stakeholder, and what an activity heatmap buckets on.

state.workflow: Interactive demo / sandbox analytics with stakeholder discovery
state.evidence: The spec says: 'Discover stakeholders with intra-viral sharing' and 'a buyer re-shares it internally, Consensus surfaces the newly discovered stakeholders'. It also says 'activity heatmaps' without naming the axes. It gives metric names but no denominators: demos sent, organic stakeholders discovered, discovery rate, views, view rate, features/sections selected, docs downloaded.
state.constraint: Schema-flexible JSON in records.data only. Discovery must be inferred from re-sharing, not declared by the viewer. Tests must freeze the clock, so a bucket must be a pure function of an event timestamp.
state.option_a: Infer discovery from the event stream: a view event carrying an upstream share reference (shared_from) from a known stakeholder makes the viewer a discovered stakeholder attributed to that sender. Bucket the heatmap on weekday x multi-hour slot derived from each event's own timestamp.
state.option_b: Declare the stakeholder at share time: recording a forward share immediately mints a discovered stakeholder. Bucket the heatmap on elapsed days since the initial send.
state.option_c: Use the CRM integration hub to discover stakeholders from the vendor's contact feed, and bucket the heatmap on buyer-group x section.

verdict.instructions: Which modelling option best fits the researched behaviour and the constraints, judging correctness, testability with a frozen clock, and reversibility?

criteria.option_a: Infer from the event stream; weekday x hour heatmap
criteria.option_b: Mint at share time; days-since-send heatmap
criteria.option_c: CRM contact feed; buyer-group x section heatmap
